articles.title: New Yankees Rumors Reveal Randy Arozarena as Target in 2026 MLB Free Agency
articles.summary: The New York Yankees are reportedly interested in Randy Arozarena this offseason.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees are reportedly interested in Randy Arozarena this offseason.

Jon Heyman of the New York Post reported Monday that New York checked in on the veteran outfielder during general manager meetings even though the team's "clearest needs are in the bullpen and at third base, in that order."

While the Yankees have other needs, they could use an additional bat in the outfield. After all, center fielder Trent Grisham is a free agent this offseason and could sign elsewhere.

If he does, New York could add Arozarena and potentially move Cody Bellinger to center field to cover Grisham's absence.

Arozarena would also be a welcome addition to the lineup.

His resume includes a Rookie of the Year, three All-Star selections and an American League Championship Series MVP. He was a back-to-back All-Star in the last two seasons with the Seattle Mariners and has become more of a power threat as his career progresses.

In fact, his 27 home runs in 2025 were a career-high, and he nearly reached that total this past season with 26. It was also the sixth consecutive season he reached the 20-homer mark during his time with the Mariners and Tampa Bay Rays.

The Yankees are also always in championship-or-bust mode, and Arozarena is a proven playoff performer. His ALCS MVP came during the 2020 season when he helped lead the Rays to the World Series, and he also helped the 2025 Mariners reach the ALCS and come just one win short of advancing to the Fall Classic.

Overall, he has slashed .292/.380/.565 with 12 home runs in 45 playoff games.

Arozarena, who led the league with 113 runs scored just last season, would surely become a fan favorite in New York if he put up postseason numbers like that. It would also help him in his pursuit of a championship ring, which is one of the only things missing from his list of accomplishments.

articles.title: New Tarik Skubal Rumors Reveal How Mets Meeting Went Amid Dodgers Buzz in MLB Free Agency
articles.summary: The New York Mets reportedly took a major step toward potentially adding the offseason's biggest prize.
articles.body:
The New York Mets reportedly took a major step toward potentially adding the offseason's biggest prize.

Jon Heyman of the New York Post reported the Mets held an in-person meeting with pitcher Tarik Skubal on Monday. While there was no word if an official offer was made, Heyman reported it "went very well" with the "expectation" the southpaw will sign somewhere before a possible lockout when the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1.

Heyman also noted the Los Angeles Dodgers, San Diego Padres, Toronto Blue Jays and two mystery teams are seen as the other contenders who are expected to be given meetings.

That New York met with him comes as no surprise, as ESPN's Jorge Castillo, Alden Gonzalez and Jesse Rogers reported Friday it was seen as the "industry favorites" to land him.

"Having a complete rotation is really important, and that includes having pitchers that successfully can get you through a playoff series," president of baseball operations David Stearns said while not specifically referencing Skubal, per ESPN. "We have seen over and over again in the playoffs that it can be constructed in a variety of different ways, and so we're open to doing it any way possible."

The ESPN report also added that the Mets see Nolan McLean and Christian Scott as the only locks for next season's rotation.

Skubal would be a significant boost for the National League East team or any other club that signed him as arguably the best pitcher in the sport.

His list of accomplishments includes two Cy Young awards, two ERA titles, a pitching Triple Crown in 2024 and two All-Star selections. He was brilliant again during the 2026 campaign with a 2.72 ERA, 0.96 WHIP and 186 strikeouts in 158.2 innings for the Dodgers and Detroit Tigers.

If New York can find a way to sign him, it will become a much bigger threat in the National League picture. That is especially true since it will also mean keeping him away from returning to the Dodgers.

It at least reached a point where it got a meeting, and now the baseball world will wait to see what comes of it.

articles.title: Ranking Diamondbacks 2B Ketel Marte's Top 6 Landing Spots Amid MLB Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Ketel Marte has a full no-trade clause, but that hasn't stopped Major League Baseball's hot stove from churning out fresh rumors about interest in the Arizona Diamondbacks' enigmatic second baseman.
articles.body:
Ketel Marte has a full no-trade clause, but that hasn't stopped Major League Baseball's hot stove from churning out fresh rumors about interest in the Arizona Diamondbacks' enigmatic second baseman.

Marte was a big topic of trade rumors last winter, in large part because that no-trade clause went into effect in April, making it something of a "now or never" situation for Arizona to trade away the veteran infielder who still has nearly $90M left on his contract.

Yet, after Marte no-showed in Boston this past August—13 months after a similarly head-scratching absence in July 2025—there's already been a lot of chatter this offseason about a Marte trade. The belief is that Arizona is at least listening to offers , if not outright pursuing them. The latest news from this past weekend is that the Baltimore Orioles "have dialogued with the D-backs regarding Marte."

If he's willing to waive his no-trade clause, who else might be looking to acquire the 33-year-old with 111 home runs and an .851 OPS since the beginning of 2023?

With Brandon Lowe, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Luis Arraez and Gleyber Torres all available as free agents, one would assume most teams with a need at second base would prefer to go that route, not needing to part with trade chips in addition to taking on a significant contract.

But how often do you get a chance to buy low on a player who has been ( per FanGraphs ) a top 20 position player in all of baseball over the past four years?

Cincinnati Reds —Matt McLain barely had a .600 OPS this past season, while Marte has a career OPS of 1.043 at Great American Ball Park. While the need is clear and the solution could be right here, would the Reds be willing to take on a $90M contract? Or do they have enough trade capital to even pique Arizona's interest?

Los Angeles Angels —If the Angels are involved in a big trade this winter, the expectation is that they'll part with Zach Neto rather than acquire someone significant. But they're turning over a new leaf under new ownership. They also had one of the worst second base situations in the majors in 2026.

Philadelphia Phillies —With Luis Arraez, Alec Bohm and Edmundo Sosa out of the picture, it presently looks like the plan is Otto Kemp at third base with Bryson Stott at second. If they traded for Marte, though, Stott was solid for the 43 games he spent at the hot corner. Are they really going to add another expensive player in his mid-30s, though?

Pittsburgh Pirates —We'll find out soon enough whether Brandon Lowe is going to remain with the Buccos on the one-year qualifying offer. If he declines it, though, second base goes from a position of strength to a major weakness. As with Cincinnati, though, it's more than fair to question if Pittsburgh would be willing and able to absorb this contract.

San Francisco Giants —Though Arizona likely wouldn't trade him within the division, the Giants are questionable at second base in what should otherwise be an excellent infield. What spending they are able to do, though, ought to be on pitching.

Current Infield Situation : 1B Willson Contreras / Jake Bauers, 2B Curtis Mead / Franklin Arias, SS Trevor Story, 3B Caleb Durbin

Hypothetical Trade : 2B Kristian Campbell and 1B Triston Casas for Ketel Marte

The Red Sox were the hypothetical landing spot numero uno for Ketel Marte last offseason. Considering second base ended up being a completely underwhelming revolving door of Marcelo Mayer, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Anthony Siegler and Nick Sogard, they probably regret not doing more to make it happen.

After watching Franklin Arias blossom into one of the top prospects in all of baseball, trading for Curtis Mead at the 2026 deadline and already signing Jake Bauers this offseason?

With a projected cash payroll already north of $209M, which is a mark they haven't had on Opening Day since 2022?

It seems like giving up anything of value to acquire Marte is no longer even close to the top of Boston's to-do list.

What Boston does have, though, is a pair of once highly-touted infielders who could use a new lease on life.

They gave Kristian Campbell an eight-year, $60M contract at the beginning of the 2025 campaign, only to watch him become a shell of the budding star who raked through the minors in 2024. Maybe they give him one more year at Worcester, since he's still only making $3M in 2027. He does become even more dispensable if they're adding Marte to the equation.

Speaking of dispensable, what possible path back to Boston does Triston Casas have now with Bauers in the fold? He hasn't played since early May 2025 due to a series of injuries that began with a ruptured patellar tendon. However, with two years of team control remaining, he could be a strategic lottery ticket for an Arizona team lacking at first base.

Current Infield Situation : 1B Ben Rice / Luis García Jr., 2B Anthony Volpe / José Caballero, SS George Lombard Jr., 3B Ryan McMahon

Hypothetical Trade : IF Anthony Volpe and LHP Ryan Weathers for Ketel Marte

With Jazz Chisholm Jr. out of the picture, the Yankees have a pretty substantial question mark at second base.

Do they sign Brandon Lowe if he declines his qualifying offer from Pittsburgh?

Maybe they bring Gleyber Torres back home, or scoop up singles specialist Luis Arraez?

Could they just let it ride with what they've got and hope this is the year Anthony Volpe finally posts an OPS north of .666?

Let's be honest, though: If they go that latter route with so many other options on the table this winter, Yankees fans would (and should) throw quite a fit.

Trading for Marte might be the best solution, provided they think he could handle the bright lights of New York without any more...unexcused absences.

With our proposed package, the Diamondbacks would be getting three years of Volpe, as well as two years' worth of Ryan Weathers—who is a bit superfluous in a Yankees starting rotation that would still be overcrowded even if he were taken out of the mix.

Buy or Sell Latest MLB Offseason Free Agency, Trade Rumors

Current Infield Situation : 1B Pete Alonso, 2B Jackson Holliday / Blaze Alexander, SS Gunnar Henderson, 3B Jordan Westburg / Coby Mayo / Christian Encarnacion-Strand

Hypothetical Trade : 2B Jackson Holliday and RF Tyler O'Neill for Ketel Marte

On the one hand, we kind of have to put the Orioles in the top five, since their reported interest in Marte sparked this latest foray into the speculative trade market.

On the other hand, would anyone have connected those dots otherwise?

With Jordan Westburg presumably returning after missing all of 2026 due to UCL surgery, the Orioles already have a surplus of viable infielders—even if they're just throwing in the towel on the No. 1 overall pick from the 2022 draft, Jackson Holliday.

If that's the case, though, could the soon-to-be 23-year-old with four years of team control remaining be the main attraction that piques Arizona's interest?

Maybe a change of scenery does the trick and awakens the force who had an OPS north of .900 in each of his first three years in the minors.

We're throwing Tyler O'Neill into this hypothetical trade, too, to help the Orioles make the finances work for the upcoming season. He's actually owed more cash in 2027 ($16.5M) than Marte is ($13.75M).

It's the $75.5M that Marte is owed from 2028-31 that the Diamondbacks are presumably trying to remove from their books, though. If O'Neill stays somewhat healthy for a change, the Snakes could certainly use one more experienced outfielder.

Current Infield Situation : 1B Spencer Torkelson, 2B Hao-Yu Lee / Max Anderson, SS Kevin McGonigle, 3B Colt Keith, UTIL Zach McKinstry / Javier Báez

Hypothetical Trade : 1B Spencer Torkelson and LHP Andrew Sears for Ketel Marte

One of the only players discussed as a trade candidate for longer than Marte is Detroit's Spencer Torkelson.

That scuttlebutt started two years ago, when the Tigers signed Gleyber Torres and looked to shift Colt Keith to first base and move on from the slugger who didn't hit much of anything in 2024.

Maybe they trade him now, though, with two years of team control remaining?

Whether it's Hao-Yu Lee moving to first base or Keith sliding across the diamond with Lee taking his spot at the hot corner, they have options. It's also plausible that either Josue Briceño or Thayron Liranzo wins the job as a rookie.

On the opposite end of the deal, Arizona would figure to be extremely interested in adding Torkelson's bat at first base. He hit 57 home runs over the past two seasons. It's presently looking like the Diamondbacks are going to enter spring training with no clue whether Tyler Locklear, Tim Tawa, LuJames Groover or Jose Fernandez offers them the least problematic best solution at that position.

Pitching prospect Andrew Sears would further sweeten the deal. He got pummeled in his 19.0 innings pitched in the majors in 2026, but he had a 2.85 ERA and a 10.1 K/9 across 259.0 innings in the minors over the past three years.

Current Infield Situation : 1B Jared Young / Mark Vientos, 2B Marcus Semien / Brett Baty, SS Francisco Lindor, 3B Bo Bichette, IF Jefferson Rojas

Hypothetical Trade : LHP Sean Manaea, IF Mitch Voit and RHP Jack Wenninger for Ketel Marte

Last winter, the New York Mets traded five years and $102.5M of Brandon Nimmo to the Texas Rangers for three years and $72M of Marcus Semien.

While moving Nimmo opened the door for both Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing to shine as rookie outfielders, Semien was a colossal disappointment. The now-36-year-old second baseman's bat had already faded in his final two years with the Rangers (.686 OPS compared to .811 from 2021-23), but New York was banking on the two-time Gold Glove recipient (including one in 2025) to improve their run prevention. Instead, he provided some of the worst defense at second base in all of MLB this past season.

Of course, this means they're pretty well stuck with the $46M left on Semien's contract. The same goes for the final year of both Jorge Polanco ($20M) and Kodai Senga ($14M).

But maybe they could talk the Diamondbacks into taking Sean Manaea's $17.25M salary to have him serve as a swingman in their pitching staff in 2027?

It wouldn't do anything to help Arizona's payroll situation in the upcoming season, but it does make them a whole lot more flexible next winter for what should be a more compelling class of free agents. They sure do need some arms after losing almost a dozen pitchers to free agency.

On the prospects side of this proposed deal, Mitch Voit was a late first-rounder in the 2025 draft who stole 45 bags with an .801 OPS this season, while Jack Wenninger would be a more enticing candidate for big-league work in 2027 if he hadn't struggled so much with walks this year.

Current Infield Situation : 1B Vladimir Guerrero Jr., 2B Ernie Clement, SS Andrés Giménez, 3B Kazuma Okamoto, UTIL Josh Smith / Charles McAdoo

Hypothetical Trade : 2B Ernie Clement and RHP Gage Stanifer for Ketel Marte

Toronto finished dead last in the majors in both home runs and runs scored and was 29th in OPS in 2026—one year removed from ranking third in OPS and fourth in scoring.

It's not exactly a secret that they'll look to upgrade that offense this offseason, or that they'll be willing to spend to do it. At any rate, their current estimated payroll is more than $60M below where it was on Opening Day this past season, so making room for Marte shouldn't be a problem.

Beyond the unknown of whether both Arizona and Marte would accept a trade, the big question is whether second base is where the Blue Jays necessarily want to make that spending—and whether they're willing to basically kick Ernie Clement to the curb after he inexplicably led the American League in All-Star votes.

Over the past three seasons, though, Marte has hit 86 home runs with an .853 OPS. Clement has a fine glove, but over the same period, he has 30 home runs and a .683 OPS.

If the already 33-year-old Marte can continue to produce at anything close to the same level, that'd be a major upgrade for the lineup.

articles.title: Buy or Sell Latest on Tarik Skubal, Randy Arozarena and Offseason MLB Free Agency, Trade Rumors
articles.summary: With MLB's collective bargaining agreement expiring December 1 and a lockout expected to follow, the offseason is picking up steam anyway. There have been a few signings and the rumors aren't stopping.
articles.body:
With MLB's collective bargaining agreement expiring December 1 and a lockout expected to follow, the offseason is picking up steam anyway. There have been a few signings and the rumors aren't stopping.

So, who's up for a round of "Buy or Sell?" on the latest rumors?

We've picked out eight rumors from the last few days that we think deserve scrutiny, though it's worth clarifying that this is not about putting the sources under the microscope. Rather, this is about the implied outcome.

For instance, if a rumor claims that Team A is interested in Player B, is it believable that a deal between the two will actually get done?

Let's get to it, starting with a certain West Coast ace who is purportedly not available in trade talks.

Is Logan Webb Totally Unavailable in San Francisco?

Nightengale is pretty unequivocal in his reporting on where the San Francisco Giants stand with Logan Webb. He writes that they will not trade him, "no matter how many teams continue to ask for the ace."

Look, you can't fault teams for asking. The 29-year-old righty has mostly been a mainstay among the best pitchers in baseball for much of this decade. He's also on a team-friendly contract that will pay out $47 million across 2027 and 2028, which is a steal for a three-time All-Star who also has three top-10 finishes in the NL Cy Young Award voting.

Right now, though, the Giants would risk selling low if they were to deal Webb. The 2026 season was not his finest hour, as injuries limited him to 27 starts and his ERA ballooned to 4.31. He especially struggled in the latter half of the year, posting a 5.89 ERA over his last 13 starts.

That the Giants should be looking to rebuild after a 97-loss season is the argument in favor of trading Webb, but every indication is that they'd rather not. Indeed, Nightengale says they're looking to add starting pitching.

Besides which, it's not like the Giants are hurting for prospects. Per B/R's Joel Reuter , they have six top-100 talents in their system.

Have the Yankees Already Nixed a Jonathan Loáisiga Reunion?

It was Heyman who reported last week that the New York Yankees were in on Loáisiga, which made for a fun little story on account of his history with the team. Now he says they "seem focused elsewhere at moment."

Loáisiga was a top-100 prospect when he came up with the Yankees in 2018, as part of a sort of second wave of Baby Bombers that also featured Miguel Andujar. His Yankees tenure peaked in 2021, when he produced 3.3 rWAR out of the bullpen. He then experienced a whirlwind between 2022 and 2025, with Tommy John surgery in 2024 in the middle of the vortex.

After reestablishing himself with a 2.42 ERA in 67 appearances for the Arizona Diamondbacks, Loáisiga would seem to be an ideal fit for a Yankees bullpen that is currently missing David Bednar and Paul Blackburn. Moreover, general manager Brian Cashman has spotlighted the pen as " our main priority ."

The Yankees always have a bunch of irons in the fire, however, and it's possible that they're not focused on Loáisiga solely because of that. Even if he's on their radar, it's a big radar.

More likely, they're focused on also bringing back Bednar and Blackburn after already re-upping with Tim Hill. And why not? For all the flak the Yankees rightfully get for their tendency to "run it back," keeping the 2026 pen together is a good idea. It had the second-lowest ERA in the league at 3.13.

Are the Orioles a Fit for Randy Arozarena and Ketel Marte?

Sources: Andy Kostka of The Baltimore Banner and Jake Rill of MLB.com

The Baltimore Orioles have been known to be on the hunt for upgrades to their outfield, and Kostka reports that Randy Arozarena is of interest to them. If so, they'd better be ready to pay up.

He is a Scott Boras client, after all, and Adam Jude and Ryan Divish of The Seattle Times heard during the GM Meetings that Boras is pushing for a six-year deal in the $150 million range. The Orioles have only gone that far for a free agent twice in their history, including for Pete Alonso just last year.

Of course, Boras wouldn't be good at his job if he didn't aim high at the outset. It's doubtful that any team will go as far as five years for Arozarena, much less six. As such, this initial demand comes off as a prelude to settling for $100 million.

With a $36 million gap between what they spent in 2026 and what they project to spend in 2027, the Orioles could do something like four years, $100 million for Arozarena and still have money left for other needs. It also may not hurt that the Orioles hold spring training in Sarasota, Florida, which is about an hour's drive from Arozarena's home in Tampa.

As for Rill's report that the Orioles are in on Marte, that largely depends on whether he wants to go to Baltimore. His 10-and-5 rights allow him to block any trade. And per Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic , the D-backs still may not have a clear idea of where Marte would go even after meeting with his agent.

Even so, a Diamondbacks insider described the relationship between Marte, the team and manager Torey Lovullo as "completely broken" to John Perrotto of FanSided. A trade would be best for everyone, and the O's are a good fit on account of their plethora of left-handed bats. For instance, a Marte-for-Jackson Holliday trade would be fun.

Is Trevor Rogers Radioactive for Certain Clubs?

Even if none of them are on Tarik Skubal's level, Trevor Rogers is part of a solid selection of free agent starters that also includes Freddy Peralta, Michael King and Sonny Gray.

Rogers has a problem, though: Out of all the starters on the market, he's the only one with a qualifying offer.

Unless the new CBA completely does away with the system, the lefty will be tied to penalties if he rejects the offer (as expected) and signs with another team. Those are especially severe for luxury tax payors, who have to give up $1 million in international bonus money and two draft picks if they sign Rogers.

To this end, Rosenthal posits that the New York Mets, Chicago Cubs, San Diego Padres and Atlanta Braves are "expected to be interested" in Rogers, but that they could prefer to sign other starters who aren't tied to a qualifying offer. He's pretty plugged-in, so this may not be idle speculation.

All four of those clubs badly need starting pitching, so this could end up being a "beggars can't be choosers" scenario for any one of them if Rogers is still there after other options come off the board. For now, though, it is plausible that they would prefer not to sign him. It's not as if he's a can't-miss talent , after all.

Should Teams Stop Asking the Rays About Drew Rasmussen?

Sources: Bob Nightengale of USA Today and Robert Murray of FanSided

In the aftermath of the World Series, Drew Rasmussen instantly became a popular speculative subject for offseason trades. Heck, MLB Trade Rumors even had him at No. 2 on their list before the Rays triggered his $20 million option.

Tampa Bay Rays president of baseball operations Erik Neander moved quickly to quiet such talk , saying that the team has "every intention" of keeping its ace for the 2027 season. Nightengale's and Murray's reporting indicates that nothing has changed in the weeks since.

Granted, you can still look back at the Rays' history and feel skeptical. They do tend to cash in on trade value once it's there, and especially if it also means saving some money. In this case, the time they ducked a $25 million salary by trading Tyler Glasnow to the Los Angeles Dodgers comes to mind.

However, the Rays weren't coming off a World Series run when they did that. Even if they're already projected to spend $16 million more in 2027 than they did in 2026, they should be able to afford that.

There also wasn't a lockout looming when the Rays traded Glasnow. There is this time around, and it's complicating the trade value of all players who are slated for free agency after 2027. Rasmussen is one of those, and the size of his salary surely only complicates things further.

Is Now the Time for a Junior Caminero Extension?

Sources: Robert Murray of FanSided and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic

According to Murray, extensions for young players in general are "something heard as possibilities" right now. Junior Caminero is among the candidates, and Rosenthal's reporting breaks the situation down in full.

Some of the intrigue comes down to timing. For players, the looming lockout is effectively a threat of future constraints on earning power. As such, the time for Caminero to maximize his future earnings may be now .

There's also the matter of the cost. Caminero has hit 87 home runs over the last two seasons, including 42 in a 2026 campaign that saw him finish second in the AL MVP voting. And he's just 23 years old.

Thus, Rosenthal's ballpark estimate for extending Caminero: "It would certainly be $200 million plus, maybe even $300 million plus."

The Rays have never signed a deal that big, but that may not be relevant in this context. They're finally due to get a new ballpark in (they hope) 2029, and owner Patrick Zalupski has teased a corresponding payroll leap into the top 15 or even the top 10 of MLB.

An extension for Caminero would essentially be a down payment on that project, and he has every reason to listen if the Rays make a good offer. There are still four years standing between him and free agency, so there's sense in striking now while the iron is hot rather than risking it going cold.

Could Freddy Peralta's Contract Blow Away Expectations?

Sticking with the Rays for one more, we turn to Bowden's rather surprising comp for Freddy Peralta's next contract: Carlos Rodón.

"Peralta is expected to get five or six years in the Carlos Rodón range (six years, $162 million)," he wrote.

For reference, B/R's Tim Kelly projects only a three-year, $73 million contract with a post-2028 opt-out for Peralta. Even a more aggressive projection from MLB Trade Rumors stops at five years and $110 million.

Granted, Evan Phillips and Jake Bauers have already beaten expectations for their contracts, which could bode well for Peralta. And while the rest of us can fret about how he only had a 4.42 ERA this year, it's an outlier relative to his career 3.71 ERA.

Teams also care about what players project to do, and Peralta showed at the end of 2026 that he deserves optimistic projections. He was terrific for the Rays in September and October, posting a 1.82 ERA over 49.1 innings.

That said, teams will also recognize that Peralta is a seasonal age older than Rodón was as a free agent after the 2022 season. Even if he matches Rodón's AAV, a five-year deal worth $135 million should be his ceiling.

Could Tarik Skubal Actually Score a $500 Million Contract?

There have been $500 million projections for Tarik Skubal before, but it's the way that Bowden framed the possibility that stands out as being slightly different:

"Teams meeting with Skubal know going in that the price will end up between $350 and $500 million depending on years, and that the final contract will ultimately break the record for starting pitchers by both AAV and total amount."

You see that? "Know." Not "expect." Not "anticipate." Know.

OK, fine. Maybe we are reading too much into that. And it's fair to have doubts whether Skubal has that much earning power. The current high-water mark for a pitcher contract is $325 million. Is he really going to reset the bar by $175 million?

Actually, it might not be that far of a reach. MLB Trade Rumors has Skubal getting to $425 million in their predictions, and they have a history of under estimating contracts for ace pitchers. In recent years, Dylan Cease, Corbin Burnes, Blake Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Carlos Rodón have all beaten their MLBTR predictions.

Besides, this could be the last chance MLB's big spenders get to make it rain without any limitations. Why leave anything to chance?

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.summary: With the MLB's top hardware all handed out now, the hot stove is starting to sizzle.
articles.body:
With the MLB's top hardware all handed out now, the hot stove is starting to sizzle.

It's still very early into free agency, but there are already moves being made—and rumblings about possible moves to come.

Let's dig into the rumor mill and guesstimate what this buzz could mean for some of the top free agents on the market.

Mets Favored in the Tarik Skubal Sweepstakes?

For a while now, it's felt as if Tarik Skubal's free agency will come down to a two-team race between the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets. But according to MLB.com's Mark Feinsand , the sentiment shared at the recent General Managers Meetings in Las Vegas was that "nearly everybody in the game expects Skubal" to wind up with the Mets.

"I don't know who else is really even in the conversation," an NL executive told Feinsand.

Skubal's list of suitors, per Feinsand, includes the Mets, Dodgers, Toronto Blue Jays and San Diego Padres. Even then, though, Feinsand basically dumped a bucket of cold water on everyone but the Mets.

The Dodgers "prefer a shorter-term deal with a higher average annual value," but Skubal "is not interested in that kind of deal." Feinsand opined that "it's hard to see Toronto topping the Mets" in a bidding war and noted that while the Padres plan to spend this offseason, they are "more likely to spread those funds around rather than making one huge splash."

Prediction: Skubal signs with the New York Mets.

A tale of two seasons thankfully ended on a high note for Fredd Peralta, as his disastrous first-half stint with the New York Mets gave way to a return-to-form run with the Tampa Bay Rays after the deadline. He had a 3.25 ERA in 10 regular-season starts after the trade, then trimmed the number to 2.95 ERA in five postseason appearances.

Teams clearly took note of the turnaround, to the point that Peralta now stands as one of the top consolation prizes for teams who miss out on Skubal (or simply lack the funds to participate in the sweepstakes). The San Diego Padres might be mulling that very move.

"The Padres have set up a meeting with Tarik Skubal but have also expressed interest in Freddy Peralta, among other free agent starters, and are open to reunions with Michael King, Nick Pivetta and Nick Martinez," ESPN.com's Alden Gonzalez wrote.

San Diego's rotation is basically a blank slate alongside Randy Vasquez, so the Padres figure to be among the most aggressive pitcher-suitors on the market. That doesn't mean they'll get Peralta (or Skubal, obviously), but they should at least be firmly in the running.

Prediction: Peralta signs with the Toronto Blue Jays.

The Baltimore Orioles' shopping list runs as long as you'd expect for a club coming off of consecutive losing seasons. That said, finding an upgrade at outfield—ideally, from a player who hits from the right side—ranks prominently among the top priorities.

And the Orioles reportedly have one candidate firmly in mind: Randy Arozarena, who's had better than 25 homers and 25 steals in each of the last two seasons.

"Two sources said the Orioles are expressing interest in Randy Arozarena," Andy Kostka reported for The Baltimore Banner .

Kostka added the Orioles have interest in bringing back Luis Robert Jr., while listing Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki as speculative fits. Baltimore, in other words, seems to have backup plans in place, which it might need since our crystal ball does not see the O's adding Arozarena.

Prediction: Arozarena signs with the Philadelphia Phillies.

articles.title: Dustin May Reportedly Lands White Sox Contract, Will Leave WS Champion Brewers in MLB FA
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers have lost another free agent with Dustin May reportedly set to join the Chicago White Sox.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers have lost another free agent with Dustin May reportedly set to join the Chicago White Sox.

Per Robert Murray of FanSided, May has agreed to terms on a three-year deal worth just over $50 million with the White Sox.

May's departure comes after the Brewers lost NLCS MVP Jake Bauers to the Boston Red Sox in free agencylast week.

It's not a surprise that both players are leaving because they were likely to be priced out of Milwaukee's range.

In the case of May, he also seemed unlikely to return because of his struggles after being acquired in a midseason trade with the St. Louis Cardinals. The right-hander had a 5.65 ERA over 36.2 innings in 10 starts after the trade.

The postseason wasn't much better for May, as he allowed seven earned runs in 11.0 innings over five appearances. He did have two scoreless outings, both one-inning relief appearances.

Overall in 2026, May finished with a 4.70 ERA in 145.2 innings across 31 starts between the Cardinals and Brewers. It was his second consecutive year with an ERA over 4.50 since returning from Tommy John surgery.

Despite those recent struggles, May is a solid bounce-back candidate for a team on the rise like the White Sox. His peripherals were better than his overall performance with a 3.63 FIP with the lowest home run-to-flyball ratio of his career in a season with at least 100 innings (9.2 percent).

The White Sox are in a position where they need both high-end starting pitching and players who can fill out a rotation. One of the problems they ran into in the postseason was a heavy reliance on relievers.

Chicago's bullpen accounted for 44.1 innings while starters logged 17.2 innings across seven games.

May will slot into a White Sox rotation led by Sean Burke. They are also planning to stretch Grant Taylor out to become a starter after he threw 84 innings primarily in relief last season.

The strength of Chicago's roster right now is the lineup, led by Munetaka Murakami and Miguel Vargas, so the rotation doesn't have to be elite to get this team back to the playoffs in 2027 after a surprise 84-win campaign last season.

articles.title: Jake Bauers, Red Sox Agree to Contract After World Series Run, Latest MLB Rumors on Deal
articles.summary: A breakout 2026 season for Jake Bauers has resulted in a new contract from the Boston Red Sox in free agency.
articles.body:
A breakout 2026 season for Jake Bauers has resulted in a new contract from the Boston Red Sox in free agency.

Per ESPN's Jeff Passan , Bauers has agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal with the Red Sox, which was formally announced on Tuesday.

After being a backup journeyman outfielder early in his career, Bauers found his footing as a 29-year-old with the Milwaukee Brewers during the 2025 season. He hit .235/.353/.399 in 85 games.

The 2026 campaign saw Bauers maintain that patient approach at the plate and add power to his game. He finished with a .266/.389/.484 slash line and 26 homers in 144 games during the regular season.

Bauers' 143 wRC+ ranked seventh among all qualified hitters. He ranked third in on-base percentage, behind Yordan Alvarez (.432) and TJ Rumfield (.390).

During the Brewers' postseason run to the World Series, Bauers became a household name thanks in large part to two plate appearances in the NLCS against the Los Angeles Dodgers.

The first was a 12-pitch walk against Yoshinobu Yamamoto in Game 2 that drove his pitch count up, resulting in the shortest playoff start of his career (2.2 innings). The second was an 11-pitch at-bat against Blake Snell in Game 3 that ended with a two-run homer to put Milwaukee up 3-2.

Bauers was named NLCS MVP thanks to a .286/.412/.571 slash line in the Brewers' four-game sweep to help them clinch their first World Series appearance since 1982.

Prior to joining the Brewers after the 2023 season, Bauers had bounced around with multiple teams as a fourth outfielder. He was originally drafted by the San Diego Padres in 2013, was traded to the Tampa Bay Rays after the 2014 season.

After making his MLB debut with the Rays in 2018, Bauers was traded to the Cleveland Guardians in December 2018. He played 117 games in 2019, didn't appear in a game during the 2020 season and was traded to the Seattle Mariners midway through the 2021 campaign.

Bauers split time in the minors with the Triple-A affiliates for the Cincinnati Reds and New York Yankees in 2022. He made it back to the big leagues in 2023, appearing in 84 games with the Yankees.

This past season, his final year of arbitration, Bauers made just $2.7 million from the Brewers. He turned out to be one of the best bargains in the sport and figures to hold a lot of value going forward with his bat-to-ball skills.

As long as the power that showed up in 2026 remains part of his game, Bauers will be a huge addition for a Red Sox team that struggled to hit down the stretch and in their brief playoff run that ended in a two-game sweep against the New York Yankees in the AL Wild Card round.

Bauers' signing is going to further speculation that a trade involving Jarren Duran could be on the horizon. The Red Sox were already crowded between first base and the two corner outfield spots.

Willson Contreras is locked in as the starter at first coming off an All-Star season. Wilyer Abreu had a breakout 2026 after being a solid starter in each of the previous two years. Roman Anthony, as long as he is healthy, might be the best hitter on the team.

That leaves at least one of Duran of Masataka Yoshida, both of whom have already been mentioned as trade candidates, potentially pushed out with Bauers coming in.

Regardless of the next moves from Boston, Bauers is a huge addition for the lineup because of his approach and ability to get on base. As long as the power he displayed last season continues going forward, this could be a bargain deal for the Red Sox.

articles.title: RHP Dustin May, White Sox reportedly agree to 3-year, $52.5M contract
articles.summary: May is the second Brewers player to leave in free agency, joining Jake Bauers, who signed with the Red Sox.
articles.body:
Dustin May is reportedly signing with the Chicago White Sox, according to FanSided's Robert Murray . Per ESPN's Jesse Rogers , the agreement is worth $52.5 million over three years.

May is the second member of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers to leave this offseason. Last week, first baseman Jake Bauers signed a four-year, $58 million contract to join the Boston Red Sox .

The White Sox enjoyed one heck of a turnaround in 2026 en route to a surprise postseason appearance and a tightly-contested division series against the AL Central rival Cleveland Guardians. But with their sudden surge out of the rebuild and into October came elevated expectations going into the offseason, as there would now be pressure on the front office to build off the newfound success and begin to construct the roster with more ambitious goals. They skipped past the usual first step for last-place clubs of becoming respectable, and instead now have the opportunity to leap straight into a group of AL contenders with the right additions made around the promising young core in place.

As evidenced by the White Sox essentially running out of pitching by the end of their series against the Guardians, the most obvious place to upgrade for Chicago this winter was going to be on the mound. But with the White Sox having such a limited history of spending aggressively in free agency, it was unclear what level of the starting pitching market they'd shop in. A pursuit of top-line ace Tarik Skubal never seemed realistic, but could they finally splurge on the next tier of starter in Freddy Peralta or Michael King? Perhaps such a pursuit is still in the cards in the coming weeks, but Chicago has at least made an early statement in committing a sizable chunk of change to May, who has tantalized for years with his raw stuff despite rarely demonstrating reliable run prevention.

May's primary selling points are his plus velocity and relative youth, as he turned 29 in September, making him one of the younger free-agent starting pitchers available. He's also coming off a career-high 31 starts and 145 2/3 innings, a welcome uptick in workload for a pitcher who had battled myriad injuries throughout his career.

More broadly, May's agreement with Chicago marks the first by any free-agent starting pitcher this offseason, which should provide an interesting benchmark for the bevy of other starters seeking multi-year deals. The merits of committing north of $50 million for May could reasonably be debated, but however you feel about May, Chicago would be best-served adding another starter or two if they want to feel good about their chances in the AL Central entering 2027.

May started the 2026 season with the St. Louis Cardinals and made 10 regular-season starts for the Brewers following the trade. During Milwaukee's postseason run, he appeared in five games, made two starts and posted a 5.73 ERA and 1.18 WHIP over 11 innings with eight strikeouts.

Injuries, including Tommy John surgery in 2021, limited May's time on the mound during his time with the Los Angeles Dodgers, who drafted him in the third round in 2016.

The 2025 season, his final one in L.A., saw May get healthy as he made 18 starts and pitch 104 innings, the most in his MLB career. In 2026, he topped that number during the regular season with 109 IP, striking out 106.

The White Sox were reportedly one of a handful of suitors of May. According to MLB Network's Jon Morosi , the Chicago Cubs, San Diego Padres and Houston Astros were also interested in the right-hander.

articles.title: Red Sox Reportedly Make Trade to Clear Roster Spot for Jake Bauers Contract in MLB Free Agency
articles.summary: Needing to clear out a roster spot before their signing of Jake Bauers can become official, the Boston Red Sox trading reliever Raymond Burgos.
articles.body:
Needing to clear out a roster spot before their signing of Jake Bauers can become official, the Boston Red Sox trading reliever Raymond Burgos.

Per Chris Cotillo of MassLive.com, the Red Sox will send Burgos to the Athletics for Kenya Huggins.

Bauers, who agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal with Boston last week, will be formally introduced by his new team at a press conference on Tuesday at 3 p.m. ET.

Boston had a full 40-man roster prior to the move, so the front office had to do something before the Bauers deal could become official.

Huggins, a fourth-round pick in the 2022 draft, had a 6.63 ERA in 31 appearances at Double-A last season.

Burgos is coming off a 2026 season in which he had a 4.22 ERA with 16 strikeouts in 21.1 innings over nine appearances.

An 18th-round pick in the 2016 MLB draft, Burgos made his big-league debut in 2024 when he appeared in one game for the San Francisco Giants.

After spending the 2025 season in the minors, Burgos signed with Guerreros de Oaxaca of the Mexican League and had a 5.25 ERA in eight innings over three appearances.

The Red Sox signed Burgos to a minor-league deal in May. He was called up in August and finished all eight games he pitched, primarily in mop-up duty, and finished with two saves.

Even with the pending trade of Burgos, the Red Sox still figure to explore the market because of their logjam at first base, DH and the outfield with Bauers coming in.

Bauers and Willson Contreras figure to split first base and DH duties. Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu seem locked in as the outfield starters.

Jarren Duran and Masataka Yoshida would seem not to have a direct path to playing time. Yoshida has to DH because his defense has been very bad throughout his MLB career.

Duran finished eighth in AL MVP voting as recently as 2024 and was worth 4.0 fWAR in 2025, but he is considered a potential non-tender candidate with the Nov. 20 deadline approaching for all pre-arbitration and arbitration-eligible players if the Red Sox can't find a trade partner after he hit .207/.266/.361 in 151 games last season.

articles.title: Seiya Suzuki Reportedly Declines Cubs Qualifying Offer amid MLB Free Agency Rumors
articles.summary: As expected, Seiya Suzuki is heading to free agency.
articles.body:
As expected, Seiya Suzuki is heading to free agency.

The star outfielder declined the Chicago Cubs' $23.1 million qualifying offer on Tuesday, per Mark Feinsand of MLB.com, and will now hit the open market as one of the more appealing bats available this winter.

Suzuki, 32, hit .270 with 26 homers, 86 RBI, 96 runs and a .841 OPS in 2026. It was his fourth straight season with 20 or more dingers, an OPS above .800 and at least 70 RBI.

That consistency, paired with a market relatively thin on quality outfielders and right-handed bats, makes him one of the more appealing free agents on the market.

As ESPN's Kiley McDaniel noted, "Among regular outfielders, he's fifth (behind Aaron Judge, Juan Soto, Ronald Acuña Jr. and Kyle Tucker) in the all-encompassing batting stat wRC+ and 12th in WAR [over the past four seasons]. Suzuki's WAR number drags a bit because his defense in right field had been league average to slightly below, but it ticked up dramatically to plus in 2026."

Or as Max Ralph of MLB.com wrote, "As Suzuki still displayed an elite plate approach (89th percentile chase rate and 91st percentile walk rate in 2026) and a better-than-average swing speed (73.3 mph), there should be little immediate concern that his offense will decline."

In other words, he could be looking at a contract that exceeds the $100 million mark or reaches five seasons, though his age may play a factor in whether he hits either benchmark. Still, a big contract is incoming, making it inevitable that he would turn down the qualifying offer.

articles.title: The Mets look like the frontrunner to land Tarik Skubal. What other teams are in the mix?
articles.summary: Skubal is the biggest prize in the MLB free agent market this offseason, but only a small group of teams will realistically make a run at the two-time Cy You...
articles.body:
In the most predictable news of this most uncertain MLB offseason , the New York Mets visited with prized free-agent hurler Tarik Skubal on Monday.

According to the New York Post, a "high-powered contingent" of club officials journeyed out to sunny Orange County, California, for a sit-down with Skubal and his agent Scott Boras. No significant details have emerged yet from the gathering and no official offer has been extended. But while New York's interest in the market's top player is far from shocking, the existence of a meeting is a sign that Skubal's free agency is picking up steam.

The overwhelming expectation across the sport is that the two-time Cy Young Award winner will sign before the current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1. That should enable the 29-year-old to break the record for the largest contract ever given to a pitcher, the 12-year, $325 million pact Yoshinobu Yamamoto inked with the Dodgers ahead of 2024. Reportedly, Skubal is set to meet with at least five additional clubs: the Dodgers, Blue Jays, Padres and two "mystery teams."

But as of right now, based on a number of conversations with industry insiders, the Mets are considered the frontrunner for the southpaw's services.

Since purchasing the club in November 2020, hedge fund titan Steve Cohen has invested more than $1.5 billion on players. Only the Dodgers have spent more. While Cohen's cash-flashing has resulted in just two postseason series wins over that span, the world's 89th richest person has shown no signs of letting up. He is set to pay Juan Soto $57.5 million next season. He's broken records before, and he'll do it again.

The Mets finished 2026 with an estimated payroll of $358 million and have around $85 million coming off the books this winter. That should give president of baseball operations David Stearns more than enough leeway to maneuver aggressively in the free-agent market.

New York's pitching staff doesn't deserve all the blame for the club's disastrous 2026 campaign, but it sure deserves a lot of it. As a collective, Mets starters finished 23rd in baseball with a 4.47 ERA. Their 9.1 percent walk rate ranked 24th. Those numbers were even uglier over the first three months, with New York's season self-imploding well before the summer solstice.

Only three rotation spots appear set for 2027. Rookie of the Year fourth-place finisher Nolan McLean and his 3.16 ERA over 179 2/3 innings is the de facto ace. Still just 25 years old, McLean seems primed to take yet another step forward next season. Two other youngsters, righty Christian Scott and lefty Zac Thornton, showed enough in '26 to pencil for '27. Highly paid veterans Sean Manaea and Kodai Senga were massive disappointments last season and could easily be pushed to the bullpen full time once the Mets make external additions.

3. There's a dearth of other obvious landing spots

Whether or not every team "can" afford to sign Skubal under MLB's current economic system is mostly beside the point. Because realistically, only a handful of clubs will meaningfully pursue the class' crown jewel. And critically, several of those big spenders already have well-paid, world-class starting rotations.

The Yankees have AL Cy Young winner Cam Schlittler and are paying Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodón a combined $90.5 million in 2027. The top of Boston's rotation looks secure with Garrett Crochet, Payton Tolle and Ranger Suarez. Philadelphia has $100 million committed to Zack Wheeler, Aaron Nola, Cristopher Sánchez and Jesús Luzardo this coming season with young buck Andrew Painter holding down the No. 5 spot.

The Cubs, in desperate need of arms, have adopted a posture of disinterest toward Skubal. The Braves would obviously love to pair Skubal with Chris Sale atop their rotation, but Atlanta hasn't given a free agent more than $75 million since B.J. Upton in 2013.

San Diego Padres: Last winter, with their ownership situation in flux, the Pads operated like paupers. But with the transition complete from the Seidler family to power couple Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones, San Diego is widely expected to reassert itself as a financial force this offseason.

Notably, the Padres' rotation is in dire straits right now, with seven of their eight most used starters hitting the open market. A reunion with free agent Michael King, who helmed the Padres' rotation this past season, makes the most sense, but signing Skubal would be quite the statement from a new ownership group that's talked a big game since taking over.

Toronto Blue Jays: The 2025 American League champs backed up that unforgettable run by backing up the Brink's truck to Dylan Cease's house to the tune of seven years and $210 million. Cease made good on that investment, finishing second in AL Cy Young Award voting in 2026. Could the Jays try to run that strategy back? Their roster has several enticing rotation options (José Soriano, Trey Yesavage, Spencer Arrighetti) but could benefit from an external addition. After such a disappointing 2026, reeling in the winter's biggest fish would be an effective way to reengage the fan base.

Los Angeles Dodgers: Do the Dodgers need Skubal? Of course not, but they didn't need him when they traded for him in August either. Reporting has indicated that Los Angeles is primarily interested in signing Skubal to a short-term, high average annual value deal. Skubal and his reps, understandably, are focused on the opposite. The Dodgers, for what it's worth, appear more focused on rejuvenating their roster with youth and on supplementary upgrades. Of course, the richest team in the game could change course at any moment and piss everyone off all over again.

articles.title: MLB qualifying offers: Randy Arozarena rejects offer, David Bednar stays with Yankees
articles.summary: Randy Arozarena will turn down a one-year deal from the Mariners to seek a massive contract on the free-agent market.
articles.body:
After turning in a fantastic walk year with the Mariners, outfielder Randy Arozarena is going to test the free-agent market. The 31-year-old outfielder was among the biggest names to reject a qualifying offer Tuesday.

He wasn't the only one. Six players who received qualifying offers from their former teams decided to reject them by the 4 p.m. ET deadline Tuesday.

Because of that, the following players are now free agents*:

• OF Randy Arozarena (Mariners) • 2B Brandon Lowe (Pirates) • OF Seiya Suzuki (Cubs) • SP Trevor Rogers (Orioles) • RP Adrian Morejon (Padres) • 1B Jake Bauers (Brewers)*

*Reports emerged Friday suggesting Bauers agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal from the Boston Red Sox. The team has yet to officially announce that contract, though that could happen soon now that the qualifying offer deadline passed.

The news doesn't necessarily come as a surprise, as those six players are expected to receive lucrative, multiyear deals on the market.

David Bednar, Ryan Jeffers accept qualifying offer

Two players, however, opted to accept the qualifying offer Tuesday. Minnesota Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers and New York Yankees closer David Bednar decided to stick around for one more season with their respective teams.

Neither player will hit the free-agent market as a result of that decision. Both Jeffers and Bednar will return to the Twins and Yankees, respectively, on one-year, $23.15 million deals.

Teams are eligible to extend qualifying offers to upcoming free agents who meet certain criteria. If a player is given a qualifying offer, that player receives a one-year deal to re-sign with their former club at "the mean salary of the league's 125 highest-paid players." In 2026, the qualifying offer salary was $23.15 million.

Players who receive a qualifying offer have until a certain date every offseason to either accept or decline that offer. If a player accepts, they return to their old team on a one-year deal at a high salary. If they reject, that player immediately hits the free-agent market, and the team becomes eligible to gain draft-pick compensation if that players signs with another franchise. The team that signs a player who rejected a qualifying offer is subject to losing a draft pick in order to sign that player. The value of that pick can vary based on how much money that team pays to sign a player who declined a qualifying offer.

Due to the various risks involved, qualifying offers are often given to players expected to receive bigger deals in free agency.

Why do players decline qualifying offers?

On the surface, a qualifying offer can look like a tempting deal for some players. Take Bauers, for instance. The 31-year-old was previously seen as a journeyman before his 2026 breakout. Given his age and lack and track record, Bauers may have faced significant questions on the free-agent market. Because of that, a one-year, $23.15 million offer — significantly more money than Bauers has ever earned in his career — may have been an alluring option.

Though Bauers would have made more money per year if he stayed with the Milwaukee Brewers, many players value long-term security over short-term deals. It also helps that Bauers will reportedly receive double that $23.15 million in his deal with the Red Sox. Bauers might be earning less each season, but he was able to get a big payday and a long-term commitment from a team.

That's exactly why many players decide to decline the qualifying offer and hit the free-agent market. There's typically more money — and more long-term security — on the table.

Can players who reject a qualifying offer return to their old teams?

Rejecting a qualifying offer isn't necessarily a bad thing for the team that extended it. Players are eligible to return to their former franchise even after declining a qualifying offer. That's exactly what happened with the Philadelphia Phillies and Kyle Schwarber last offseason. The slugger declined a qualifying offer from the team, but opted to return on a long-term contract later in the offseason.

In that instance, the Phillies were not required to give up — and did not receive — draft-pick compensation after re-signing Schwarber.

That opens the door for any of the remaining five 2026 qualifying-offer players to return to their old franchises, but not until seeing what the rest of the league is willing to pay for their services.

articles.title: David Bednar, Yankees Agree to New Contract, Star Closer Avoids 2026 MLB Free Agency
articles.summary: The New York Yankees announced closer David Bednar accepted his qualifying offer to return to the team for the 2027 season on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees announced closer David Bednar accepted his qualifying offer to return to the team for the 2027 season on Tuesday.

He's now set to receive $23.15 million for his 2027 campaign, per ESPN's Jeff Passan .

USA Today's Bob Nightengale reported that Bednar and Minnesota Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers were the only two MLB players to accept the qualifying offer before Tuesday's deadline at 4 p.m. ET.

Bednar has been with the Bronx Bombers since they acquired him in a trade with the Pittsburgh Pirates during the 2025 season.

The right-hander spent two years with the San Diego Padres and just over four years on the Pirates to open his MLB career, earning a pair of All-Star nods in 2022 and 2023.

Last season, Bednar was a key piece of a Yankees bullpen that ranked No. 2 in the majors with a 3.13 ERA overall.

In 64 appearances, he recorded 35 saves to go along with a 2.47 ERA and 1.038 WHIP. Opposing batters hit just .205 with a .563 OPS against Bednar.

He particularly thrived throughout the second half of the year, owning a 2.15 ERA in 27 games after the All-Star break. Bednar also racked up 31 strikeouts compared to eight walks in 29.1 innings of work across that span.

The Yankees have focused on bringing back their own relievers during the offseason, as they previously agreed to a one-year contract worth $2.25 million with Tim Hill on Sunday.

As New York attempts to clinch a fourth consecutive playoff appearance in 2027, Bednar will be back in the mix as well.

articles.title: Why Astros' Bryan Abreu might be a fantastic sleeper free agent target
articles.summary: The Astros' free agent reliever might be of great interest this Fall.
articles.body:
The Houston Astros are undergoing some major change this offseason, and one of the biggest is the looming departures is Bryan Abreu, their right-handed reliever.

After a shaky 2026 season, Abreu is set to hit the open market and can now sign with any team in Major League Baseball. But considering his 3.73 ERA this past season is a far cry from his 2022-through-2025 production, there are questions about Abreu.

However, as ESPN's Kiley McDaniel outlined, Abreu is actually one of the more fascinating free agent options for teams this Fall, as he might be the ultimate sleeper free agent reliever this offseason.

Why Bryan Abreu might be a big sleeper this free agency

"Because he's still in his 20s and he still struggled with some mechanical and confidence issues this season, there's a clear case that a new coach, a change of scenery, and rebuilding his mechanics could help him become his former self as soon as next season," McDaniel writes.

Abreu's fall-off might be to the benefit of whichever team takes a chance on the reliever, as his upside is incredibly high when he's pitching at his best.

After his fastball dropped in velocity this past season, and seeing his strikeout and walk rates go in the wrong direction, teams would have reason to be cautious with Abreu.

But whichever team makes the move to sign the reliever will have a chance to benefit greatly from taking a chance on Abreu if they can get him back to his former self.

There's very little risk with adding Abreu, especially if the market isn't forcing his deal upwards of $50 million, like McDaniel believed Abreu could've reached if it weren't for a down 2026 season.

With just a one-year, $10.5 million contract projection, Abreu could be a massive steal in free agency if a team with a good pitching coach can help Abreu fix the issues that derailed his 2026 season.

Abreu is a sleeper free agent this offseason thanks to his high upside at what should wind up being a big discount due to a down 2026 season.

While he might not return to the Astros, some contender might be getting a massive steal in free agency if they can sign Abreu to a cheap contract this Fall.

articles.title: Report: Mets meet with Tarik Skubal, MLB’s top free agent
articles.summary: NEW YORK — The Mets have officially entered the Tarik Skubal arms race. Team officials met with Skubal in Southern California on Monday, according to reports...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — The Mets have officially entered the Tarik Skubal arms race.

Team officials met with Skubal in Southern California on Monday, according to reports, as the coveted left-hander explores his options in free agency.

Skubal, who turns 30 on Friday, is MLB's top free agent after he followed up his back-to-back American League Cy Young Award seasons from 2024-25 with another dominant campaign this year.

In 2026, Skubal went 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158 2/3 innings over 26 starts with the Detroit Tigers and Los Angeles Dodgers.

A client of super agent Scott Boras, Skubal is expected to command a historic contract approaching or even exceeding $400 million.

The deep-pocketed Dodgers, who acquired Skubal in a midseason trade with Detroit, are considered among the favorites to sign the decorated hurler. The Toronto Blue Jays and San Diego Padres have also shown interest in Skubal, according to The Athletic.

"It's very clear that there is a dominant, strong, Sku-Bull market," Boras said last week during a pun-heavy press conference at the GM meetings in Las Vegas.

"It's pretty clear that teams are not devoid of pursuing their championship fortunes. They understand there's only one Tarik card."

Whomever signs Skubal will have to be comfortable with his health, as the left-hander missed six weeks before the All-Star break due to an operation to remove a loose body in his prized throwing elbow.

Still, there should be no shortage of interest in the ace, who, since 2024, leads MLB starters with an 18.0 WAR (wins above replacement) and ranks second with a 2.42 ERA.

Skubal also ranks fourth in innings pitched (546.0) and in strikeouts per innings (10.80) during that stretch.

Under president of baseball operations David Stearns, the Mets typically haven't shopped at the top of the free-agent starting-pitching market, though they showed a willingness to make an exception with a massive bid for Yoshinobu Yamamoto in 2023.

Then 25, Yamamoto ultimately signed a 12-year, $325 million contract with the Dodgers. In terms of guaranteed money, that deal remains the record for a pitcher, which Skubal seems all but certain to break.

Hanging over this offseason is the Dec. 1 expiration of baseball's collective agreement, with a lockout practically guaranteed to follow. At that point, teams will not be able to negotiate with free agents until a new CBA is reached.

Teams must weigh the uncertainty of what the next CBA will look like when they consider whether to invest in free agents such as Skubal between now and Dec. 1.

MLB owners seek a salary cap, while the MLB Players Association staunchly opposes one.

It's unclear if or how big-money contracts would be grandfathered in under a new CBA with more restrictive payroll rules.

But teams also won't want to miss their chance to sign Skubal, who is a clear tier above the other free-agent pitchers such as Freddy Peralta, Michael King, Sonny Gray, Nick Martinez and Clay Holmes.

Adding Skubal this offseason would transform a Mets rotation that features promising young arms in Nolan McLean, Christian Scott and Zac Thornton but that could use a top dog after the team's back-to-back playoff misses.

MLB's award season came to a conclusion on Tuesday when the Silver Slugger Awards were handed out.

The Silver Slugger awards go to the best offensive player at each position, voted on by MLB managers and coaches. Each team has four votes.

First Base: Pete Alonso, Baltimore Orioles

Second Base: Chase Meidroth, Chicago White Sox

Shortstop: Bobby Witt Jr., Kansas City Royals

Third Base: Junior Caminero, Tampa Bay Rays

Outfield: Randy Arozarena, Seattle Mariners

Outfield: Chase DeLauter, Cleveland Guardians

Utility: Kevin McGonigle, Detroit Tigers

Catcher: Gabriel Moreno, Arizona Diamondbacks

Shortstop: Elly De La Cruz, Cincinnati Reds

Outfield: Pete-Crow Armstrong, Chicago Cubs

Outfield: Jackson Chourio, Milwaukee Brewers

Outfield: James Wood, Washington Nationals

Designated Hitter: Kyle Schwarber, Philadelphia Phillies

Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez led the majors in batting average (.316), slugging percentage (.601) and OPS (1.033) while hitting 42 homers, making the American League MVP an obvious choice for Silver Slugger.

New York Yankees designated hitter Ben Rice had a tremendous breakout season with 41 homers and 97 RBI, but that wasn't quite enough with Alvarez posting monster numbers.

It was also no surprise to see the National League MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong, make the list. The Chicago Cubs star hit 45 homers while slashing .280/.372/.570 and stealing 41 bases.

Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani's three-year streak of Silver Slugger awards came to an end at the hands of Kyle Schwarber, who was tied with Crow-Armstrong for the most homers in baseball (45).

The World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers led the majors in batting average (.258) and OBP (.341) while collecting the second-most runs (832), which led to a handful of their players landing a spot on the list.

But the Chicago Cubs took home the team award in the National League thanks to their 220 home runs, 850 runs and a .251 team batting average.

The Houston Astros may have gotten bounced from the postseason quickly, but their offense during the regular season was lights out as they bashed 226 homers and scored 734 runs.

articles.title: Alex Rodriguez Reveals Surprising Reaction to Losing Mets to Steve Cohen After Failed 2021 Bid
articles.summary: MLB legend Alex Rodriguez tried to buy the New York Mets in 2021, but was outbid by Steve Cohen.
articles.body:
MLB legend Alex Rodriguez tried to buy the New York Mets in 2021, but was outbid by Steve Cohen.

Cohen purchasing the Mets for a then-record price of $2.4 billion is something Rodriguez is forever grateful for.

"We took a run at the Mets; I thank God every day for Steve Cohen for buying the Mets," Rodriguez said Tuesday at the Axios BFD conference, per The Athletic's Mike Vorkunov . "I send him a Christmas card every year."

After coming up short trying to purchase the Mets, Rodriguez, alongside Wonder founder Marc Lore, instead purchased the Minnesota Timberwolves for $1.5 billion

"I grew up a Mets fan — 1986 was like the greatest year of my life," he said. "I thought '86 was great, and obviously '09, when we (the New York Yankees) won the title, was even greater. But I think the NBA presents an incredible opportunity. We caught it at the right time. I think we're fortunate to do it as a COVID buy. We bought it for $1.5 billion. Today, most teams average over $5 billion."

The investment is already paying off, as the Timberwolves were valued at $4.5 billion earlier this year when Lore sold his stake to Marc Stad. That number is sure to get even bigger over the next few years.

articles.title: Former Yankees slugger Mark Teixeira celebrates as Congress’s version of Mr Irrelevant at office lottery
articles.summary: Mark Teixeira drew chip No. 105 of 105 in the House freshman office lottery, earning Congress's "Mr. Irrelevant" tag and a playful un-victory lap.
articles.body: Retired MLB slugger Mark Teixeira began his baseball career sitting at the top of the draft boards, so Washington wasted no time humbling him Tuesday. Incoming members of Congress have zero seniority, so they draw numbers from a box to set the draft order for picking Capitol Hill offices. On Tuesday, the newly elected Texas Republican pulled chip No. 105 out of 105, giving every other rookie first dibs while leaving him with the scraps. Even with the dead-last pick, Teixeira hopped on X to voice how happy he was to earn the spot. "I consider it an honor to have the last pick of offices and let all my fellow freshmen go ahead of me," the ex-New York Yankee posted. Finishing dead last makes Teixeira Congress's version of "Mr. Irrelevant," leaving him with whatever leftover office nobody else wants for the next two years. DEMOCRATS FACE DAUNTING CONGRESSIONAL BASEBALL GAME STREAK AS EX-MLB GREAT EYES GOP ROSTER SPOT But Teixeira handled it like a vet. His draw sparked cheers and a bipartisan standing ovation, so Teixeira took a playful "un-victory lap" around the room, jogging past new colleagues and trading high-fives and fistbumps. "Sometimes you prepare, you put the work in, and it’s just not your night," Teixeira told reporters afterward. FROM LOCKER ROOMS TO CONGRESS: JAY FEELY LATEST ATHLETE SEEKING TO TAKE LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP TO CAPITOL HILL Being picked dead last is new territory for a guy the Texas Rangers drafted fifth overall in 2001. Over 14 MLB seasons, Teixeira crushed 409 home runs, won five Gold Gloves, made three All-Star games, and captured a 2009 World Series ring in New York. After retiring in 2016, Teixeira worked at ESPN before jumping into Texas politics. In August 2025, he launched a Republican run for Texas’s open 21st Congressional District, promising to fight "for the principles that make Texas strong and America exceptional." EX-YANKEE MARK TEIXEIRA UNLOADS ON MLB FOR TRYING TO 'SILENCE' CHRISTIAN FAITH With President Trump's endorsement, Teixeira cruised through his March primary and beat Democrat Kristin Hook on November 3 with 55% of the vote. "I’m not going to Washington for myself, but rather to be a strong, responsive voice for every family in this district." He will just have to make that voice heard from the worst office in D.C. articles.summary: With the 2026-27 MLB offseason underway and all of the late-season prospect graduations in the rearview, it's time for an update to our organizational top 10 prospect lists and farm system rankings.
articles.body:
With the 2026-27 MLB offseason underway and all of the late-season prospect graduations in the rearview, it's time for an update to our organizational top 10 prospect lists and farm system rankings.

A tier system was used to help differentiate the varying levels of prospect talent:

Tier 1: Nos. 1-25 on B/R's Top 100 prospects list . These are the cream of the prospect crop—players viewed as potential future superstars.

Tier 2: Nos. 26-50 on B/R's Top 100 prospects list. These prospects are potential All-Star-level talents, but with at least one minor question in their profile.

Tier 3: Nos. 51-100 on B/R's Top 100 prospects list. These prospects might have recently broken out, are still in the lower levels of the minors or are former Tier 1 or Tier 2 prospects whose stock is down.

Tier 4: Nos. 101-200 among prospects, in no particular order, who have the highest likelihood of entering the Top 100 in the future.

Tier 5: Everyone else. Organizational depth, one-tool standouts, Quad-A guys, teenagers with an extremely limited track record in the lowest levels of the minors, you get the idea.

A player must not have surpassed the rookie-eligibility limits (130 at-bats, 50 innings pitched, 45 days on an active roster) to be included in these rankings.
